title: How a hand-drawn timeline keeps its labels inside fixed boxes

steps.title: Can a hand draw a diagram without moving its labels?
steps.line: A timeline names four periods but gives none of them positions.
steps.caption: A simulated hand makes every stroke a little different. If it also decided where the words and boxes went, the timeline could lose its structure. This example starts with four named periods and no positions; the next steps lay out their boxes before drawing them by hand. The pele page uses the same separation for four charts, though this timeline is our own model, not its code.
steps.picture: Code, 5 lines; “The page’s four plates”, 4 labelled values.

steps.title: The layout engine fixes every box, marker and label
steps.line: The engine places every box; the drawing never moves one.
steps.caption: On the page pele lays the chart out, measuring each label with Hershey letter widths so the boxes fit the hand lettering. Here Agentic Mermaid does the layout with Inter’s widths, so the lettering is fitted into the boxes later. The dimension gives one event box’s width in stage units.
steps.picture: Timeline: 4 periods; Code, 5 lines; A dimension line marked “2.96 units”. Measured: Midnight Wick trimmed. New in this step: Timeline: 4 periods; A dimension line marked “2.96 units”.

steps.title: Fixed layout marks guide the hand’s later strokes
steps.line: Every later stroke is drawn from these marks alone.
steps.caption: Like the page, which flattens pele’s SVG into marks a script can select, the drawing reads the layout back: 40 outlines, 13 filled shapes and 8 words. A blue construction pencil traces them first, and every later stroke is drawn from these marks alone.
steps.picture: Code, 5 lines; The timeline’s layout traced in thin blue construction pencil: 4 period boxes, 4 event boxes, their markers and strings, the rail and an empty box where each word will go; 1 label. New in this step: The timeline’s layout traced in thin blue construction pencil: 4 period boxes, 4 event boxes, their markers and strings, the rail and an empty box where each word will go; 1 label.

steps.title: The hand strays at most 0.002 units from the line it follows
steps.line: A damped spring chases the line; tremor shakes it.
steps.caption: The pen is a mass on a damped spring, 8 Hz with damping 0.6, chasing a point that moves along the line at 1.2 units a second, shaken by tremor of up to 0.006. Close on the Midnight marker, the spring smooths the tremor into slow wobbles about the blue ring.
steps.picture: The timeline’s layout traced in thin blue construction pencil: 4 period boxes, 4 event boxes, their markers and strings, the rail and an empty box where each word will go; Close on the Midnight marker: the pen’s ink following the blue ring, wobbling gently about it. New in this step: Close on the Midnight marker: the pen’s ink following the blue ring, wobbling gently about it.

steps.title: The made-up world is drawn far to near, around the chart
steps.line: Hills, sea, lighthouse, gulls: never on paper the chart owns.
steps.caption: Hills, sea, a rock with its lighthouse and beam, then gulls: 6 layers, far to near. The chart and the title own the paper inside the dashed lines, with a 0.12 margin, so the scenery is cut away there: 0 scenery points land on owned paper.
steps.picture: The timeline’s layout traced in thin blue construction pencil: 4 period boxes, 4 event boxes, their markers and strings, the rail and an empty box where each word will go; Close on the Midnight marker: the pen’s ink following the blue ring, wobbling gently about it; Dashed red outlines round the chart and the title: the paper they own; Around the blue construction lines, a world drawn far to near: hatched hills on the left, a sea of short blue strokes, a rock and a striped lighthouse on the right with a yellow beam, and three gulls; the paper the chart and the title own is left bare. New in this step: Dashed red outlines round the chart and the title: the paper they own; Around the blue construction lines, a world drawn far to near: hatched hills on the left, a sea of short blue strokes, a rock and a striped lighthouse on the right with a yellow beam, and three gulls; the paper the chart and the title own is left bare.

steps.title: The chart is drawn last, then its words
steps.line: Objects, then words; no ink strays over 0.005 from its mark.
steps.caption: Periods become planks, events become tags hung on strings, and the rail becomes a rope: 13 objects drawn on the laid-out marks, no ink more than 0.005 units from them. Hershey letters come last, inside the boxes the layout gave; a second drawing changes the strokes and scenery without moving the chart’s laid-out boxes.
steps.picture: The timeline’s layout traced in thin blue construction pencil: 4 period boxes, 4 event boxes, their markers and strings, the rail and an empty box where each word will go; Close on the Midnight marker: the pen’s ink following the blue ring, wobbling gently about it; Around the blue construction lines, a world drawn far to near: hatched hills on the left, a sea of short blue strokes, a rock and a striped lighthouse on the right with a yellow beam, and three gulls; the paper the chart and the title own is left bare; Light pencil tints on the chart: ochre on the 4 period planks, blue on the 4 event tags, every word’s box left clear; The timeline drawn as objects in warm-black ink over its blue construction: 4 periods as planks, 4 events as tags on strings, marker rings and a rope rail; Every word of the chart in Hershey single-stroke letters, and the title “The lamp-keeper's night” in the sky.
